reason: Tests that each IPC channel has an action or a reason to deny it and that pairing channels are not offered.
Test harness opens the Rust app-action service with scripted effects and preferences.
Tests action approval, refusal, notification and journal outcomes using the app-control rig.
Exercises merge commits, predicted conflicts and dirty-parent refusal against Git repositories.
Tests when a merged session branch may be deleted from origin, including squash merges.
Creates temporary Git repositories and worktrees and prepares stale-parent and squash-merge fixtures.
Tests worktree removal and retention, including archiving ignored files before removal.
Asserts the commits, changed files and parent checkout state reported by branchFacts.

git.mergeCheck and git.mergeBranch bracket an independently supervised pre-merge hook; a failed post-merge hook reports without undoing the merge. Discard uses the inspected tip, calls the host archive/removal claim's prepare before git.discardRemove and settles that claim with the outcome. Neither the hook lease nor that claim belongs to a restarted core (§1.3c).
Tests session visibility, permissions, opening and delivery through AgentControlRuntime with host dependencies.

fs.stat follows links for a scheduled wake's session file and an explicitly requested local spawn folder. The host keeps the caller's path spelling and never stats a paired folder locally. Wake receipts, parent registration, window and pool ownership are read in the same turn (§1.3c).
MAIL_KINDS is tool schema vocabulary; MailDelivery is the host callback type. agentctl/service/mod.rs calls Rust delivery_for before mail_attached; the stock bridge tests supply example frames.
Exercises agent-control commands across sessions, asks, visibility, branch operations and reports using a test host.

The host pushes its synchronous tab, parent and window snapshot before asking the core to act on it. Its retry timer reopens a dead core from outside. Zod owns field errors and Date.parse; the core owns schedule action constraints (§1.3a,c).
Compares documented tool names, parameters and enum values against the host tool definitions.
Tests ordering and refusal when delivering notes, attachments and answers to an open question.

Hub batch, §1.3(c): sidecar-pool.ts and remote/host-services.ts own the open question and plan claims. TargetAnswer claims before its first await, then attaches the note and answers the same claim. Move the transaction with those owners; never interpose an RPC before the exclusive claim.
Tests tool registration, accepted arguments and exclusion of account or permission controls.

Core validates schedule action/field combinations before dispatch. Stock reads tool definitions synchronously at set_host_tools; Zod field constraints and JS number/JSON coercions stay with that schema.
Tests guarded project renaming and collision handling when the server refuses a name.
Registers the client callbacks for upkeep.renameAmbiguous and returns the Rust rename report.
Tests which journal replies become redacted conclusions and how the pass maps them to projects.
Sends journal and prompt callbacks plus cursor state to care.backfill and copies back the returned memo.
Tests which care unit runs per tick, when unfinished units resume and when failed units retry.
Native readiness starts care after five minutes and schedules the repeat. The client supplies current per-tick host settings and exposes summary and undo to the page.
Exercises memory configuration, token reads and HTTP results against controlled server responses.

aimemory owns HTTP, including health checks. §1.3: server() reads current URL/dataDir synchronously for each caller; token/status/health also report when the core itself is unreachable, which only its caller can observe.
Checks the omp launch environment and arguments before and after configuring model spending.

Core reads journal and prompt facts through the stock worker. Main supplies the installed omp launch environment, credit preferences, current settings and a launch-wide repair claim; injected test drivers answer explicitly requested fake asks.
Tests which page a curation judgment retires, including its successor and skipped projects.
Passes page, judge and rules callbacks, limits and dry-run options to care.curate and returns its report.
Checks the smol invocation, prompt input, result accounting and command failure behavior.
Forwards the omp launch specification, message and working directory to upkeep.runSmol.
Starts a loopback HTTP server backed by test-provided request handlers.
Tests retirement for deleted paths, partial disappearance and unchanged references against Git checkouts.
Passes the repository runner, project and flagged versions to care.freshness and applies the returned version map.
Exercises memory IPC handlers, including background refresh and retry without blocking the caller.

Memory IPC validates incoming requests and the loopback console address. clipboard.writePassword hands the host clipboard write and conditional expiry to the shell; no clipboard contents are read back into Node.
Tests stock omp capture with terminal wiring and with the root supplied by OMPdesk.
Checks pair batching, model cost reporting and abstention on an unparseable or failed answer.
Production care/units.rs chooses the native judge chain. Only tests call these typed clients; the core skips empty batches and disabled Jev before requesting a launch.
Implements fake page and conclusion HTTP routes over an injected memory store for sync tests.
Checks that the bundled memory CLI has no upgrade command or upstream release fetch.
Tests incremental term counts, cursor resets and preservation of the prior index after a failed read.
Checks session naming, dry runs and idempotence when retitling pages.
Sends the client callbacks, locale and dry-run flag to upkeep.retitle and returns the report.
Tests staging and setup of the bundled server, ownership of its extension root and startup ordering.

The core owns readiness and maintenance clocks. SetupRunner still launches setup --yes with isolated Windows handles outside core's lifetime. The yaml reader distinguishes an absent list from an explicit empty list; Rust applies precedence. Receivers: shared setup supervisor and host config reader. The launch host reopens the service after core loss.
Declares the macOS staging directory key and the signing requirement derived from the pinned certificate; it does not stage or verify a binary.
Exercises paired memory stores, including no-op repeat rounds and preserving concurrently changed host pages.

The core owns sync rounds and cursors. §1.3(d): the stock bridge shares the same conclusion redactor; do not fork its privacy rules in Rust. Receiver: remote-web for the RemoteDevices host-link request.
Checks learning from paused conversations and which pages upkeep writes or skips.
Native readiness schedules repair and upkeep and cancels pending ticks on pause. The repair claim belongs to this app launch, not to a replaceable core; the client reads current host settings.

Shell updater batch, §1.3a,b: a synchronous table, not an I/O unit. Detection, command planning and CliUpdater share CLI_TOOL_SPECS; relevantTools preserves the caller's display order. Move the table with these readers.
Tests attribution of CLI installs to Homebrew, Bun and npm using their actual directory layouts.

ext.binaryFacts resolves package shims and returns their manager, writable target and installed manifest version. The shell updater (§1.3c) supplies the login PATH and probes live vendor CLI versions with its command runner.
Checks package-manager executable selection, argv and environment for version checks and upgrades.
ext.cliWaitsForIdle and ext.updateRunning decide whether an update must wait. Shell updater batch, §1.3a: CLI and MCP still share synchronous owner-specific command builders and the tool catalog.
Exercises provider filtering, supervised updates and post-update detection using controlled dependencies.

Core scans the Mac for a running CLI before an update. Shell updater batch, §1.3a,c: the Settings IPC snapshot must return before the rescan settles; one state owner schedules checks, records results and queues setup's installer.
The backend supplies already-visible host facts at the pool event and forwards outside calls. The core projects socket state both for a resolved target and for numbered updates.
Checks launcher contents, PATH updates and when a packaged install may replace a launcher.

control.installCli writes the launchers; the startup adapter supplies the local platform and bin directories, appends the latter to the host PATH, and logs a failed install without stopping app startup.
Drives the CLI with arguments and stdin and checks caller identity, text output and JSON output.
Supplies a fake control backend, temporary endpoints and a line-oriented client for socket tests.

Hub batch, §1.3(a,c): control-socket/index.ts computes the random pipe or short Unix socket before its first await. sidecar-factory.ts can already read the published endpoint for a spawn while prepareDir runs. Move naming with controlEnvFor's synchronous consumers.

Hub batch, §1.3(a,c): sidecar-factory.ts and terminal/ipc.ts read controlEnvFor at spawn time; sidecar.ts and stock-helper.ts strip inherited variables synchronously. The native spawn owners must take all of these reads before the endpoint state moves.
Tests live subscription boundaries, sequence ordering and turn-end events over a socket connection.

Hub batch, §1.3(c): ipc.ts calls startControlSocket without awaiting it. The endpoint is set before directory/token preparation and withdrawn on failed listen or close. Move startup with the spawn-time readers in sidecar-factory.ts; Rust already prepares the directory, token and listener.
Tests request routing, successful frames carrying tool errors and unknown-session responses.
Exercises socket handshake, caller defaults and tool calls over real connections.

Restarts the listener after core loss, releases outside callers, fences late replies by listener epoch, and takes its synchronous pool snapshot before numbering a push (§1.3c). The core computes the reported statuses.
Verifies that replies to remote-byte and memory-sync questions go only to the core generation that asked.
Benchmark of a synchronous hub call that publishes an item; not application startup code.
Exercises nested calls, synchronous questions and asynchronous answers on the hub connection.
Starts a socket worker, blocks synchronous calls on Atomics, dispatches nested questions and rejects pending calls on connection loss.
Assigns port IDs and snapshot sequence numbers, retries timed-out held calls, and fences callback answers to the originating generation.
Exercises real core startup, requests, exit handling and generation fencing.
Spawns and stops ompdesk-core, frames binary and JSON traffic, times out or cancels requests and waits for process-group exit.
Retries a failed core open while wanted, backing off from one second to thirty seconds.
Advances the Rust manual clock and Vitest timers together for deterministic tests.

disk.locateCaches, cacheHolds and clearCache own lookup policy, limits and tool execution. Node supplies the login-shell PATH and tool environment. Receiver: the disk-care runner with its remaining host.

disk.readRunState/saveRunState restore and atomically persist completed runs. DiskCare synchronously publishes running, joins concurrent callers, and reads live removal claims and the shell HTTP cache during a pass. Receiver: disk runner with the tab and shell owners (§1.3c).
Tests removal of regenerable dependencies and build outputs while preserving hand-made directories.
Exercises cache size thresholds, clearing and disabled Bun caches.
Builds temporary Git repositories, worktrees and files and installs setup and teardown hooks for disk-care tests.
Tests retaining worktrees whose checkout or attribute rules prevent guaranteed byte-for-byte restoration.
Compares restored bytes for CRLF, LF and mixed files or verifies that the worktree was retained.
Tests archive rollback on partial removal and restoration of staged versus unstaged edits.
Tests deletion and retention of scratch folders for held sessions and files cited in replies.
Tests preserving worktrees changed after listing and saving one whose contents stayed unchanged.
Exercises usage measurements, saving and restoring idle worktrees, and retaining ones still in use.

Core owns saved.json, recovery copies and fenced filesystem mutations. Main supplies the last live removal claim, the stock redactor and the restore hook. Receiver: checkout and tab-spawn owners (§1.3c).

Rust checks links, idle age, copies of moved sessions and process facts before sweeping. §1.3: Node checks SessionProcesses.held() again immediately before dispatch and updates the ownership records read synchronously by SessionScratch.open().
Tests reuse of directory measurements, changed subtrees and hard-link deduplication.

The core owns walks, breakdown, expiry and the retained tree. DiskCare reads sizes.reused and sizes.work synchronously to log the completed pass; if core cannot open the reading, the client requests full walks.
Checks actual activity timestamps from stock-named session folders and tracked, untracked and non-regenerable ignored files.

Core reads activity, process folders and bounded file bytes. Main applies the same stock redactor to staged and working bytes and checks occupancy in the current removal claim. Receiver: the checkout owner (§1.3c).
Test coverage for stock SDK skill discovery and prompt cost.
Test coverage for ECC pack pin and file integrity.
Test probe launches a stock SDK session to measure skill visibility, slash commands and context cost.
Tests inventory row order, project scoping, install methods and skipped linked plugins.

Calls ext.seeds with the inventory and resolved binaries. The core builds project keys and selects targets. The adapter attaches the binary the updater already holds without sending it back over the pipe.
Wraps ext.* requests to the Rust core in the updater step's call fence and returns the result.
Shell IPC batch, §1.3a,c: GET returns the current rows before its rescan settles; NOW accepts only a key already in the same updater's rows. Move both handlers with the updater's state.
Checks ownership of npm, Bun, Homebrew and Python installs and the reasons other binaries are skipped.

ext.binaryFacts owns package layouts, script detection, venv versions and write access. The shell updater (§1.3c) resolves its launch PATH and queries the Python environment only for a pip console-script entry point.
Checks generated check and upgrade commands for package managers, runners and Python environments.
ext.pipLatest and ext.registryLatest parse check output. The shell updater owns the shared synchronous CLI/MCP package-manager plan and command runner (§1.3a,c); move both callers together.
Tests classification of bundled, remote and package-runner MCP launches and pinned versions.
Forwards configured servers to ext.mcpClasses for classification.
Tests which package-owner and executable combinations must wait for the running server before updating.
ext.defersWhileRunning and ext.updateRunning check the install method and scan the Mac. No live process command lines leave the core.
Tests initial inventory, project-scoped rows and keeping existing rows when inventory refresh fails.

Core classifies inventory and checks running MCP servers. Shell updater batch, §1.3a,c: IPC validates requested keys against live rows, setup owns the install queue, and the hub consumes reload decisions for live tabs.
Test coverage for declaration span and drift detection.
Test coverage for Lean module and proof trust auditing.
Test coverage for statechart rule parsing and validation.
Test coverage for TLC property coverage and failure reporting.
Test coverage for toolchain install locking and recovery.
Test coverage for TLC configuration matrix parsing.
Test coverage for code reference tag parsing.
TLA+ job lease and fencing model used by tests.
Captured TLC config error output for parser tests.
Captured TLC deadlock output for parser tests.
Captured TLC invariant output for parser tests.
Captured TLC lasso output for parser tests.
Captured TLC parse error output for parser tests.
Captured TLC pass output for parser tests.
Captured TLC temporal output for parser tests.
Test coverage for SANY semantic failures and real TLC findings.
Test coverage for real TLC setup and mutation detection.
Test coverage for stock SDK discovery of the formal skill.
Test harness writes a temporary Bun script and captures its exit status and output.
Test coverage for mutation detection with a fake checker.
Test coverage for formal skill uniqueness across pack updates.
Test coverage for schema validation and report rendering.
Test coverage for Lean trust and other audit regressions.
Test coverage for TLA normalization and sharded checking.
Test coverage for per-concern findings and report generation.
Test coverage for statechart comparison command output.
Test probe resolves formal skill resources in a stock SDK session and reports prompt context.
Test coverage for TLC output statistics and trace parsing.
Test coverage for toolchain asset pins and installation.
Test coverage for verification manifest and example handling.
Forwards account checks, Git identity, logout, switching and repository star operations to gh.authCheck, gh.authIdentity, gh.authLogout, gh.authSwitch and gh.star.
setup.appleDeveloperDir checks Apple's git stub without opening its install dialog. The shell batch owns the IPC handlers and wires loginEnv to the stock PTY; GH_BROWSER must remain noninteractive.

Shell GitHub login batch, §1.3a,c,d: stock PtySession owns the terminal. The service advances one live handle's output offset; cancel marks that handle killed before asynchronous disposal. Move the handle with login state; do not start a second PTY.
Exercises signed-out, unavailable and authenticated gh states and login flows against a fake executable.

Shell GitHub login batch, §1.3a,c: cancelLogin synchronously retires the active flow and cancels setup's gh install if that flow started it. Login start, account switching and shutdown share this state. Move with setup cancellation and the IPC handlers.
Writes a fake gh executable and seeds account records for sign-in tests.

Stock reads attachments and journals mail. Before sending, Zod enforces path XOR image index and the shared encoded image limit. Those checks have no I/O; agent_control_turn also projects person === true rather than returning a raw reply (§1.3b,d).
Tests creating, overwriting, renaming and protecting agent definition files in test directories.

fs.agentFile authorizes direct paths and owns file mutations. Stock supplies the directories and validates Markdown. Main reads existing regular files without a size cap or a second whole-file wire buffer; the page shares template and name rules (§1.3d).
Tests applying plan and goal decisions and routing the associated stock commands.

Hub batch with the spawn-bound dispatcher (§1.3b,c): only the decision read gets a 3 s bridge deadline after connection. Applying a goal waits for stock's acknowledgement and stdout flush. Disconnect before the decision means unavailable; failure applying it keeps the decision's latency/model. Undo suppresses future decisions before dropping a goal; end does not.
Tests read-only ahead/behind counts and refusals for invalid roots and option-like refs.
Invalid root/ref must fail before looking up Git for git.autopilotBranchStatus. The bridge allowlist and the local-window-only set_autopilot refusal have no I/O apart from dispatch (§1.3b).
Tests merging stock state with bridge extras, fast-mode handling and defaults when the bridge is down.

omp.pluginCount runs stock's plugin list in the tab's workspace and returns only the count. sidecar.guiBridge forwards maintenance abort, forced tool, context report and share preview. Stock owns live composer state; main combines its optional replies and maps busy clears to errors (§1.3b,d).
Tests message and command ranking, fenced quote exclusion and handoff fallback for copy targets.
The dispatcher rejects an unknown method before contacting the bridge; the live grant or revoke receives the caller's params. The allowlist has no independent I/O (§1.3b).
Tests updates and owner notifications for a configured MCP server.

Hub's spawn-bound dispatcher takes the ten no-argument lookups: get_skills, get_hooks, get_context_files, get_prompt_templates, get_mcp_servers, get_plugins, get_marketplaces, get_gui_themes, get_agent_definitions, get_agent_authoring. Strip only type/id, not extra fields. sessions.journalTail checks the saved prefix; stock selects the child and reads its messages. MCP changes notify other sessions only after success.
sidecar.guiBridge reads worktree lifecycle settings from the requesting spawn. Main dispatches SCM and PR commands and verifies repository ownership before restoring a worktree.
Tests net tracked changes, rename counts and treatment of untracked or binary files in real checkouts.
Forwards repository reads to git.*. git.diff validates the path before reporting missing git or reading the checkout.
Tests macOS gh discovery with a temporary shell and Homebrew bin directory.
Tests core gh stdout, exit and timeout behavior and verifies token values do not escape into errors or logs.
Tests rediscovery after a missing binary, spawn diagnostics and git executable selection.

Core supervises every Git and gh command. Main selects the launcher and login PATH, fences the request against the current serial-chain step before sending it, and keeps onEnded until its child exits (§1.3c). macOS developer-directory lookup is cached with that launcher.
Injects Git repository selectors and verifies reads and writes stay in the intended checkout unless explicitly overridden.
Tests GitHub request validation, quiet gh invocation and classification of missing remotes versus a signed-out user.

gh.github executes the validated request. The host checks shared repo and host syntax before looking up gh (§1.3d). For a Windows verbatim UNC share root, Node dirname returns the server path while Rust Path::parent returns None. Keep path.resolve and dirname together for clone admission and its errors.
Tests project identity and worktree classification for ordinary, Autopilot and agent checkouts.

git.cachedProjectOrigin checks folder presence and the native cache before the host resolves git. git.projectOrigin coalesces misses and canonicalizes the checkout; only shared page naming and the uncached git.originFacts client remain.
Tests path containment, ref validity and worktree slug generation.
Host callers synchronously validate refs, test containment and derive a worktree slug. None reads the filesystem or invokes Git (§1.3a,b).
Compares the gh pr create arguments and resulting PR number with stock behavior.
Exercises gh.prDraftPrompt with a disposable checkout, the real Credit use wrapper and a stand-in model run. Covers a policy change during lookup and redaction of error output.

gh.prDraftPrompt reads git and renders the prompt. The tab's guarded omp.run reads Credit use immediately before spawning the model (§1.3c); draft output is parsed where it arrives. PR number/review validation and stock bridge checkout remain.
Tests independent repo locks, serial mutations per repository and fencing of work from a stopped holder.
Tests branch mutations, occupied branches and conflict continuation or abort against real repositories.
Tests working-tree and index effects of staging, unstaging, discard and other SCM commands.

Core validates selected paths and runs Git. Main's fenced-fs admits each untracked-file removal against the live lock signal (§1.3c): a core cancel frame can arrive after Stop. The 247 s Git deadline ends before removal; the 20 min holder deadline spans both. Stock commit-message generation uses the tab's guarded omp.run.
Tests worktree exit choices, branch movement and dirty versus ignored files in snapshots.

Supplies the exit policy to git.sessionWorktreeSnapshot and uses the checked native removal plan under the repository lock. The lifecycle caller still asks the person and checks a fresh fingerprint before removal; compare native-root-mini-intake's worktree_lifecycle/ candidate against those contracts before further reuse.
Integration fixture drives stock omp to test worktree paths, checkout removal, session movement and PR metadata.
Builds and copies reusable temporary Git repository, remote and session-worktree fixtures.
Tests comparison against the merge base and remote default branch, including main and detached HEAD exclusions.
Delegates the whole comparison to the Rust core method git.unlanded through coreGit.
Tests include patterns, ignored and tracked file handling and the worktree seeding size budget.

git.worktreeSeed and git.worktreeHook find the seed and hook. The independent --supervise process runs and logs the hook. Local batch retains preparation/merge wrappers and attaches the active repo-lock lease to the standalone child (§1.3c). prepareWorktree combines seed failures with the later hook result; describePreparation synchronously formats local and paired host results.
Tests real Git creation and removal, occupied folders and branches, exact branch names, exhaustion, rollback guards and checkout spelling.

fs.stat checks the base folder under the active step before Git lookup. git.worktreePlan preserves checkout spelling; git.worktreeAdd chooses the first free path and branch. The host validates the shared branch prefix and stock location, locks the repository and invokes preparation. Removal resolves Git before checking confinement: missing Git keeps its uncoded error; an outside path with Git available still fails worktree_outside_root (§1.3c,d).
Tests restoration of stock blob references on subagent and bridge transcript reads.

Stock projects saved transcripts before the worker reply. Subagent reads still resolve missing bytes through the live tab's bridge; remote-web's ImageBlobCache.resolve needs the original object sites in the current turn (§1.3c). No whole-transcript RPC.
Tests duplicate local handler refusal and which GUI or stock commands the registry claims.

mergeHandlers refuses duplicates at startup; localHandlerFor must select a handler before forwarding to stock. The async response wrapper has no I/O and only LocalCommandError contributes a code (§1.3a,b).
The live stock judge owns the model call. A failed bridge read is a successful unjudged or unavailable answer, not a command error; this projection has no independent I/O (§1.3b,d).
Tests which successful MCP operations propagate a server-specific or full reload to other sessions.
Tests filtering stock plugin doctor output and confirms that only the host, not a local handler, installs omp updates.

omp.pluginDoctor and omp.checkUpdate execute and project stock reports. Hub's spawn-bound dispatcher takes browser_relay_start, browser_relay_stop, get_security_dashboard and get_ssh_hosts: forward every field except type/id. The validation follow-up still goes to the live stock session.

Hub batch with the spawn-bound dispatcher: get_plan_mode and get_delegation forward every field except type/id. Resume refreshes the limit before sending stock goal resume; creation/replacement sets the requested limit before starting an idle objective turn. Bridge and stock replies must come from the captured clients, not a later spawn (§1.3b,c).
Tests bridge routing, invalid draft flags and handling of suggestion and inline completion commands.

sidecar.guiBridge reads suggestion state. Parameterized calls enforce request-ID and title lengths, plus stock's shared refresh reasons, draft limit and child cap before sending; a validator alone has no I/O (§1.3b,d).
Tests prompt provenance validation and which person-typed messages are noted to the bridge.

noteTypedPrompt samples isRunning before sending a person's steer. Its 500 ms timer bounds the caller's wait, not the command: the bridge may still record the typed text afterward. Keep the sample with the live sender (§1.3c).
Drives edits through the real Rust sidecar, checks chip identity across queue updates, and verifies that direct stock commands still bypass GUI edits.
Tests stock archive requests, redaction, removal of non-text entries and cleanup of the original file.

archive.prepare reserves a private output. The stock bridge redacts before replying; archive.discard verifies the exact reserved path and receipt across core restarts. Main validates replies and keeps the receipt off the page.

sidecar.guiBridge forwards copy targets and last link. Import validation, source_unavailable mapping and merging stock's stats and bridge history have no independent I/O (§1.3b). The live session owns the importers, local:// root and completion registry.
Renames synthetic sessions through the core with a stand-in stock CLI; checks argv, stdin, matched replies, missing files and the single restore retry.
omp.renameStoredSession checks the file and runs stock's fixed offline rename RPC in the temp directory; main supplies only the resolved launcher and environment.
Tests paged transcript reads, stale snapshot cursors and retries when a live tail changes.

Hub batch with sidecar: BridgeRelay fences each stock replay by tab, seq, generation and spawnId. Cursors, shrinking and retry belong with that transaction; the per-bridge tail cache returns the same page object for the same version, limit and image form (§1.3a,c). Stock owns replay and session mutations (§1.3d).
Tests model catalog availability without optional metadata and merging stock and bridge account data.

remotebytes.signInCancel sends the timed denial to stock's loopback callback. Relay setup shares the synchronous URL parser (§1.3a). sidecar.guiBridge supplies settings and model metadata. Joining logout accounts to stock's usage reply has no independent I/O (§1.3b,d).

Before yielding, loadBuiltinNames caches the pending lookup under this spawn's bridge. Stock alone advertises builtin names and aliases: sending an unknown slash as a prompt could invoke a model. Keep admission and the send with the spawn (§1.3c,d).
Tests reading journal deltas with tail tokens and resetting when a journal is replaced.
Defines stock, bridge and handler contracts plus the coded LocalCommandError wrapper; no independent command implementation.

fs.stat checks the path stock resolved before /move. The host refuses streaming moves and checks the resulting session cwd. Only stock can resolve its live session paths, change cwd and reload the associated settings (§1.3d).
Test coverage for pinned Ponytail documents and license.
Test coverage for Ponytail hook registration in stock omp.
The core probes Windows battery presence. Keep the platform power handles with LidAwake: index.ts disposes them before will-quit returns (§1.3a,c).
Test coverage for lid hold recovery and AC/work transitions.
The host/work wrappers and will-quit share the live backend; dispose calls releaseNow before returning. Move with the shell quit owner (§1.3a,c).
The synchronous quit path kills this caffeinate handle; pmset has no time limit while every core request has a deadline. Move with the shell power owner (§1.3a,c).
Test coverage for Windows powercfg parsing and restoration.

Async AC reconciliation and synchronous quit restoration read one saved previous value. Each of the three powercfg calls at quit may take 5 s; the synchronous core hub allows 2 s. Move both paths together (§1.3a,c).
Test coverage for pstack pack pins and integrity.
Test coverage for mail trigger cursors across relaunch.
Fake mailbox server supplies scripted IMAP exchanges to tests.
Test coverage for filesystem changes across relaunch.
Test coverage for branch moves against a real repository.
Test coverage for GitHub event baselines across relaunch.
Test coverage for IMAP exchanges against a fake server.
The native email trigger reads the mailbox in process. This typed client exposes the same read to the Settings account test without a second IMAP implementation.
Test coverage for configuration-keyed marks across relaunch.

Rust owns live sources, recursive watches, polls and marks. Main supplies the installed git/gh runner and mailbox connection, observes pool activity and reads tab ancestry in the same turn (§1.3c). Receiver: the pool and machine launch owners.
Test coverage for session event triggering and filtering.
Test coverage for text clipping at capture limits.
Test harness observes real schedule runs and marks with temporary repositories, synthetic mail, a fixture gh executable and a controlled session pool.
Test observer records the state sent to a window; no production schedule state mirror.
Test coverage for live trigger reconciliation on schedule edits.
Asks setup.appleDeveloperDir for the fixed xcode-select -p probe; the git trampoline, GitHub sign-in and setup use their original deadlines.
Tests release selection and checksum lookup for the supported archives against a test mirror.
Forwards release lookups to setup.resolveArchive, setup.resolveAgentDesktop and setup.resolveTailscale and translates lookup errors.
Real core file operations and a delayed or lost reply exercise restore, competing installs, stale backups and the setup queue.
Rust inspects and moves the launcher without replacing another file. Main holds the setup step until it has settled the repair and keeps the attempt identity across a lost reply.
Tests managed-only agent-desktop detection, version probing and minimum version handling.
Tests discovery of Homebrew's gh when the login shell does not supply its directory.
Checks Bun presence against the installed omp package's minimum Bun version.
Checks classification of Git shell failures, including the Mandatory ASLR signature.

setup.toolVersion probes the five located tools; setup.probeOmp, pickAgentDesktop and appleDeveloperDir select their runtime. Shell setup batch (§1.3c) retains the first-resolution gate, spawn PATH and Git shell diagnosis beside its repair and prefs.
Tests streamed progress, SHA-256 verification and cleanup of rejected downloads.
Forwards setup.download with cancellation and adapts setup.downloadProgress events and checksum errors to the caller.
Tests the scope of Git mitigation changes, quoting and recorded prior state for undo.

Shell setup batch: setup IPC accepts only an explicit fix or undo action; the existing Windows path saves prior settings through setup's prefs. Move with that authorization and restoration state, not as a separately callable privilege-changing operation.
Opt-in Windows test of changing and restoring the Git mitigation without altering unrelated mitigations.
Checks the setup IPC channels and rejects unknown retry items or Git mitigation actions.
Shell IPC batch, §1.3a,c: GET and CANCEL read SetupService immediately. RETRY validates a known item and returns while the service reports progress. Move these handlers with that service.
Exercises updates of the selected omp installation rather than unrelated executables on PATH.
Checks PATH refresh against the real core, plus synchronous managed paths and Git Bash selection.

setup.registryPath queries and parses the machine and user registry values. After it returns, refreshPath binds variables from the current process.env and publishes PATH synchronously; managedToolEnv and cli-install share the same synchronous merge (§1.3a,c).
Checks the selected installer methods, generated commands and unsupported or already-present tools.
ext.binaryFacts identifies the npm install behind omp. Shell setup batch keeps synchronous plan and manual-step selection with SetupService, the installer and its cancellation slot (§1.3a,c).
Tests streamed output and the outcomes for success, nonzero exit and spawn failure.
